questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: Sunray appearance in osteosarcoma is due to: (AIIMS Nov 2014)
questions.explanation:
Sunray appearance/sunburst/spiculated appearance - Calcification along the Sharpneys fibres can be seen in any malignant lesion but usually osteosarcoma.
Periosteal reaction is an indicator that disease is destroying the bone.
Types of Periosteal Reaction:
No reaction: Tuberculosis of bones do not usually have a periosteal reaction.
Narrow zone of activity, e.g. Solid periosteal reaction is seen in benign lesion like, Benign tumors or Pyogenic Osteomyelitis. In case of osteomyelitis the periosteal reaction is seen on day 7 to 10th.
In malignant lesions there is wide area of activity, e.g. Onion peel/codmans triangle and sunray appearance.
Onion peel or lamellated appearance- Seen in any malignant or chronic lesions but usually ewings sarcoma.
Codmans Triangle- Triangular bony growth seen at angle of lifting of periosteum it can be seen in any malignant lesion but usually osteosarcoma.

Reference: Page 15, Section: Types of Periosteal Reaction

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: A child with injury in hand with glass pieces next investigation would be: (AIIMS Nov 2014)
questions.explanation:
X- rays are usually the first radiological investigation done in orthopedics and its uses involves screening of Cortex and Marrow.
Glass pieces are visualized on X- rays due to presence of lead in them.

Reference: Page 14, Section: ROLE OF IMAGING IN ORTHOPEDICS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: Dense regular connective tissue fibres are seen in all except: (AIIMS Nov 2014)
questions.explanation:
Periosteum has two layers outer Fibrous layer (non- functional layer) and inner Cambium layer (Cellular layer/active layer).
It does not contain dense regular connective tissue as seen in tendon, ligament and aponeurosis.

Reference: Page 15, Section: Periosteum

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: Developmental Dysplasia of Hip (DDH) best diagnostic modality is: (NEET Pattern 2014, May AIIMS 2012)
questions.explanation:
If the question is asked about Investigation of choice for DDH than MRI > USG will be the order as MRI will be more useful for assessment of complete disease spectrum, management and complications of DDH.
USG in DDH: Evaluation of cartilaginous femoral head prior to appearance of ossific nucleus, subluxation, dislocation, pulvinar or inverted labrum, hypoplastic ossific nucleus, acetabular dysplasia and ossification. The findings in USG are subjective and are not as specific as MRI.
Thus if the question is asked for screening of neonatal hip or hip instability than USG is investigation of choice.

Reference: Page 17, Section: MRI in Developmental Dysplasia of Hip (DDH) & USG in DDH

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: 4-year-old girl with fever and mass in thigh, on her X-ray there is periosteal reaction and destruction of bone. Next investigation to be done in this girl is: (AIIMS Nov 2013)
questions.explanation:
Remember that radiological diagnosis in cases of infection and tumors is suggestive never diagnostic.
Diagnostic is always tissue diagnosis.
Tumors and infection can mimic each other (clinically and radiologically), e.g. Osteosarcoma and Ewings sarcoma are two tumors that mimic osteomyelitis. (Both have accompanying fever and increased local temperature).
Tumors and bone infections are usually metaphysical and both need tissue diagnosis for differentiation.
Thus, Culture is gold standard for infection Histopathology is gold standard for tumors So rule is Culture all biopsies, biopsy all cultures.

Reference: Page 17, Section: Remember that radiological diagnosis in cases of infection and tumors is suggestive never diagnostic

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: A 10-year-old obese child from endocrinology department was referred to emergency for a painful limp with hip pain which of the following investigation is not required: (AIIMS Nov 2013)
questions.explanation:
Order of Investigations in any inflammatory Joint Swelling: X-ray, MRI, Aspiration by USG (X-MAS).
This is a Obese Limping child with hip pain the possible differential diagnosis will be Osteomyelitis (X-MAS), Septic arthritis (X-MAS), Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (X-MRI), Transient synovitis (X-MAS).
Hence CT will be least preferred. Previously CT Scan was carried out for SCFE but now MRI has replaced its indication.

Reference: Page 18, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: 4-year-old child complains of pain and swelling of right tibia on evaluation patient has high ESR, leucocytosis and on X-ray tibial lesion best investigation is: (AIIMS Nov 2012)
questions.explanation:
Tumors and bone infections are usually metaphysical and both need tissue diagnosis for differentiation.
Culture is gold standard for infection Histopathology is gold standard for tumors.
So rule is Culture all biopsies, biopsy all cultures. That is whenever you obtain any sample from a suspected case of tumor or infection divide it into two parts send one for culture and other for histopathology.

Reference: Page 17, Section: Remember that radiological diagnosis in cases of infection and tumors is suggestive never diagnostic

questions.explanation:
Periosteal reaction is an indicator that disease is destroying the bone.
In case of osteomyelitis the periosteal reaction is seen on day 7 to 10th.
In malignant lesions there is wide area of activity, e.g. Onion peel/codmans triangle and sunray appearance.

USG in DDH: Evaluation of cartilaginous femoral head prior to appearance of ossific nucleus, subluxation, dislocation, pulvinar or inverted labrum, hypoplastic ossific nucleus, acetabular dysplasia and ossification.

Reference: Page 17, Section: 1c labelled bone scan

questions.stem: 45-year-old female has history of slip in bathroom complaints of pain right hip, tenderness in scarpa triangle and normal X-ray. Next investigation is: (May AIIMS 2012)
questions.explanation:
This case refers to post-traumatic pain in proximal femur, scarpa triangle refers to area of femoral neck and for stress or occult fracture of neck femur where traumatic marrow edema is seen - MRI is investigation of choice.
Any occult fracture (not visualised on X-ray) e.g. Fracture neck femur - MRI is investigation of choice.

Reference: Page 16, Section: Please Note

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: Tuberculosis of spine best diagnostic modality is: (May AIIMS 2012)
questions.explanation:
Tissue diagnosis is always preferred over any radiological diagnosis hence CT guided biopsy to obtain tissue and than further investigations to grow the organisms is the preferred approach.
Many make a mistake of marking MRI as the answer please remember that MRI is best radiological investigation but best investigation overall for infections or tumors is always biopsy.
CT Guided biopsy through the transpedicular route is a good procedure to obtain tissue from the lesion as Gold standard is always growth of organism on culture medium by biopsy thus it will be more reliable than radiological investigations.

Reference: Page 18, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 29, Section: Radiological Image Feature

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: Multiple Bone metastasis are diagnosed by: (AII2011/AIIMS Nov 2010)
questions.explanation:
It can pick up tumors that go from one bone to other, i.e. bone to bone metastasis. BONE: Bone to bone/Osteosarcoma/Neuroblastoma/Ewing sarcoma (maximum incidence).
PET- CT and Bone scan for multiple lesions (PET- CT is better than Bone Scan).

Reference: Page 17, Section: 1c labelled bone scan & Page 17, Section: Bone Tumors

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 1: Imaging for Orthopedics
questions.stem: Best investigations for multiple bone metastasis: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
PET CT: Position emission tomography + CT Scan for whole body. It is a combination of 2 modalities.
18 F Deoxy glucose uptake by tumor cells (as they have anaerobic metabolism) and CT scan for all viscera so it can indentify unknown primary. (Bone Scan the uptake is by osteoblast and PET Scan by tumor cells).
Thus PET- CT is more useful than Bone Scan as it can indentify primary and is more specific for tumor cells.

Reference: Page 17, Section: PET CT

Pyogenic Osteomyelitis on X- rays will show loss of soft tissue planes after 24- 48 hours. (1st change).

questions.stem: All are true about chronic osteomyelitis except: (NEET Pattern 2013)

options.text: Cloaca is an opening in involution

questions.explanation:
Sequestrum: Avascular piece of bone surrounded by granulation tissue, it is pathognomonic of chronic osteomyelitis. It acts as nidus of infection and is most common cause of non- healing sinus in chronic osteomyelitis.
Involucrum is dense sclerotic new bone surrounding the sequestrum formed from deep layers of stripped periosteum (usually obvious by the end of 2nd week).
If infection persists, pus and tiny sequestrated spicules of bone may continue to discharge through perforations in involucrum (cloacae).

questions.stem: True regarding acute osteomyelitis in a child: (PGI June 05)

options.text: Diagnosis by X- ray shows periosteal reaction in 8- 10 days after onset
There is tenderness at the site
Antibiotic therapy should be at least for 6 weeks
Salmonella is the most common cause

questions.answerText: Diagnosis by X- ray shows periosteal reaction in 8- 10 days after onset; B. There is tenderness at the site; C. Antibiotic therapy should be at least for 6 weeks
questions.explanation:
Pyogenic osteomyelitis on X-ray in 24-48 hours will show loss of soft tissue planes (earliest change on X-ray). Day 7 to 10- solid periosteal reaction (earliest bony change on X-ray).
Presenting complaints are Fever (>38.3°C), swelling of the limb, pain, systemic symptoms and increased levels of Total leucocyte counts, ESR and CRP.
IV antibiotics until condition begins to improve or CRP values return to normal, usually for 2 weeks. There after antibiotics are given orally for another 4 weeks.
The most common organism is staphylococcus aureus.

Reference: Page 22, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 19, Section: Clinical Feature and Investigation & Page 20, Section: Treatment

Classical Brodie's abscess looks like a small walled off (Sclerotic margins) cavity in bone with little or no periosteal reaction.
It usually involves long bones (metaphysis or diaphysis) e.g. Upper end tibia.

questions.stem: Deformity in transient synovitis of hip: (NEET Pattern 2013)
questions.explanation:
In any type of synovitis, the joint is held in Flexion, abduction and external rotation because in this position the joint capacity is maximum. (so stretching due to effusion is minimal), thus causing least pain.
Difference between Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis (Both have flexion abduction and external rotation at hip).

Reference: Page 23, Section: TRANSIENT (TOXIC) SYNOVITIS OF HIP & Page 24, Section: Difference between Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Infection of Bone and Joints
questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 2: Infection of Bone and Joints
questions.stem: Septic arthritis is diagnosed by: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Diagnosis: X- rays are usually normal or may indicate soft tissue swellings, MRI may show effusion, synovitis or cartilage destruction and aspiration of joint will help to confirm the diagnosis by culture and sensitivity and can also help to differentiate from transient synovitis.
Ultrasonographic guided aspiration of hip joint (for cytological, histological evaluation and culture sensitivity of aspirate) is the best way of making definitive diagnosis and differentiating septic arthritis and transient synovitis.

Reference: Page 23, Section: Diagnosis & Page 24, Section: Difference between Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Infection of Bone and Joints
questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 2: Infection of Bone and Joints
questions.stem: A 4/m complaints of high grade fever, decreased appetite and pain right hip. On examination he has dehydration/ tenderness in scarpa triangle/swelling in right hip region, flexion, abduction and external rotation at hip/absent movements in right hip region. On X-ray there is mild increase in medial joint space. Diagnosis is: (AIMS MAY 2009)
questions.explanation:
Difference between Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis:
Symptoms: Septic Arthritis - Severe (Toxic child); Transient Synovitis - Mild.
Movements: Septic Arthritis - Absent; Transient Synovitis - Mild Reduction.
Age: Septic Arthritis - 0-5 years; Transient Synovitis - 6-12 years.
ESR: Septic Arthritis - Markedly increased; Transient Synovitis - (n) to mild increase.
WBC: Septic Arthritis - Markedly increased; Transient Synovitis - (n) to mild increase.

Reference: Page 24, Section: Difference between Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis

Age: Septic Arthritis - 0-5 years; Transient Synovitis - 6-12 years.
Transient synovitis: It is common cause of hip pain and limping in children 6 to 12 years of age.

Reference: Page 24, Section: Difference between Septic Arthritis and Transient Synovitis & Page 23, Section: TRANSIENT (TOXIC) SYNOVITIS OF HIP

questions.stem: Transient synovitis (toxic synovitis) of the hip is characterized by all of the following, except: (AIMS May 2006)

options.text: ESR and white blood cell counts are usually normal
Ultrasound of the joint reveals widening of the joint space
The hip is typically held in adduction and internal rotation

questions.answerText: The hip is typically held in adduction and internal rotation
questions.explanation:
In any type of synovitis, the joint is held in Flexion, abduction and external rotation because in this position the joint capacity is maximum. (so stretching due to effusion is minimal), thus causing least pain.
A recent history of an upper respiratory tract infection, of viral origin is usually present.
The white blood cells (WBC) count, C- reactive protein level, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) usually are with in normal limits.
Ultrasound reveals mild effusion and widening of joint space.

Reference: Page 23, Section: TRANSIENT (TOXIC) SYNOVITIS OF HIP

options.text: Kanavel's Sign are seen in this condition
Kanavels sign are Pain/Flexion/Uniform swelling/ Percussion tenderness
Causative Organism is same as in felon

questions.explanation:
Kanavels signs are seen in infectious tenosynovitis. They are tenderness over flexor tendon sheath on percussion (most significant sign) flexion posture, i.e. rigid positioning of finger in flexion, pain on attempts to hyperextend the finger (earliest most important sign) uniform swelling involving entire finger.
Most common organism is S. aureus.

questions.explanation:
Since patient has paraplegia with Dorsal Kochs. Decompression will be performed.
Stage Wise Treatment of Potts Spine:
Stage 4: ATT + Decompression and bone grafting
Indications of surgery in any disease of spine: Deterioration in neural or clinical status on treatment; No improvement in neural or clinical status after conservative trial of 3-4 weeks or Bowel bladder involvement.
Surgical options for most of the cases are Anterior decompression + bone grafting or Anterolateral decompression + bone grafting.

Reference: Page 29, Section: Stages of TB Spine with Neural Deficit & Treatment of POTTS SPINE

questions.stem: Investigation of choice for spinal tuberculosis usually is: (NEET Pattern 2013)
questions.explanation:
MRI is one of the best radiological investigation for Potts Spine (showing soft tissues, cartilage and marrow changes), remember that radiological picture always lags behind the biological process which is already more progressive.
CT Guided biopsy through the transpedicular route is a good procedure to obtain tissue from the lesion as Gold standard is always growth of organism on culture medium by biopsy thus it will be more reliable than radiological investigations.

Reference: Page 29, Section: Radiological Image Feature

questions.stem: Poor prognostic indicator of Potts paraplegia: (NEET Pattern 2013)
questions.explanation:
Prognostic Factor:
Better Prognosis: Partial involvement, Shorter duration, Slow onset, Early onset, Younger age, Good general condition, Active disease, <60 degree kyphotic deformity, Normal cord on MRI, Wet lesion.
Poor prognosis: Complete (grade IV), Longer (>12 months), Rapid, Late onset, Older, Poor, Healed, >60 degree, Myelomalacia/syrinx (cord damaged), Dry lesion.

Reference: Page 30, Section: Prognostic Factor

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Tuberculosis of Bone and Joints
questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 3: Tuberculosis of Bone and Joints
questions.stem: All are true about spinal tuberculosis except: (NEET Pattern 2013)
questions.explanation:
Back pain, Usually minimal, is the Commonest symptom. (1st symptom).
So dorso lumbar region is the most commonly involved segment. (Remember it is dorsolumbar region and not dorso lumbar junction).
The Tubercular spread to spine usually takes place from Lungs>lymph nodes that it is that it usually secondary.
The prominence of single spinous process is called as knuckle and this is usually not seen in tubercular spine, prominence of 2-3 spinous process is angular kyphosis which is commonest in tuberculosis because of 2 contiguous vertebra involved with paradiscal destruction.

Reference: Page 28, Section: TUBERCULOSIS OF SPINE-POTT'S SPINE & Page 29, Section: Clinical Feature

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Tuberculosis of Bone and Joints
questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 3: Tuberculosis of Bone and Joints
questions.stem: False about Pott's spine: (NEET Pattern 2012)

options.text: Back pain is an early symptom
There is disk space narrowing on X-ray

questions.explanation:
So dorso lumbar region is the most commonly involved segment. (Remember it is dorsolumbar region and not dorso lumbar junction).
Back pain, Usually minimal, is the Commonest symptom. (1st symptom).
The next radiological feature of spinal tuberculosis is reduction of intervertebral disk space and osteoporosis of two adjacent vertebrae sometimes with fuzziness of the endplates.
Patient is treated by Anti Tubercular therapy, spinal brace and rest. Patient is followed on with complete neural examination and if progress is good than continued on non-operative management but if indications of surgery exist than he needs to be operated.

Reference: Page 28, Section: TUBERCULOSIS OF SPINE-POTT'S SPINE & Page 29, Section: Clinical Feature, Radiological Image Feature, Treatment of POTTS SPINE

questions.stem: Anterolateral decompression (ALD) and Anterior decompression (AD) for Potl's spine all are true except:

options.text: ALD and AD results are the same
ALD position of patient is right Lateral
ALD Laminectomy is always a part
ALD part of ribs is removed and spinal nerves exposed.

questions.answerText: ALD Laminectomy is always a part
questions.explanation:
Surgical options for most of the cases are Anterior decompression + bone grafting or Anterolateral decompression + bone grafting and both have similar success rates.
Structures removed in Anterolateral decompression are part of rib, intercostal nerves, one side transverse process, one pedicle and small part of vertebral body.
These surgeries are carried out in right lateral position (right side down left side up) approaching the spine from left side as the vessel handled is aorta on left side which is thick muscular vessel with more resilience to handling pressure as compared to vena cava which is friable to handle.
Posterior structures like Lamina are never removed because disease destroys anteriorly and if surgeon destroys posteriorly than there will be instability.

options.text: Multiple myeloma is seen in more than 55 years age and above

questions.answerText: Multiple myeloma is seen in more than 55 years age and above
questions.explanation:
Multiple myeloma: Lumbar vertebrae. Its peak incidence is in the fifth to seventh decades with a 2:1 male predominance.
Osteosarcoma: Onset can occur at any age; however, primary high-grade osteosarcoma occurs most commonly in the second decade of life.
Chondrosarcoma: It occurs over a broad age range, with peaks between 40 and 60 years for primary chondrosarcoma and between 25 and 45 years for secondary chondrosarcoma.
Osteoclastoma: They typically occur in patients 20-40 years old, and there is a slight female predominance.

questions.stem: Active benign tumor (Enneking) all are true except: (AIMS May 2011)
questions.explanation:
Benign lesions have narrow zone of activity. Zone of activity refers to area of destruction and periosteal reaction around the lesion.
Stage 2. Active: lesions also are intracapsular, but are actively growing and can cause symptoms or lead to pathological fracture. They have well- defined margins on radiographs but may expand and thin the cortex. Usually they have only a thin rim of reactive bone and narrow zone of activity. An example is Aneurysmal bone cyst. Treatment usually consists of extended curettage.

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: True about simple bone cyst: (NEET Pattern 2013)

options.text: Present as well demarcated radiolucent lesions

questions.answerText: Seen in children, B. Present as well demarcated radiolucent lesions; C. Pathological fracture seen. Cysts are metaphyseal.
questions.explanation:
Unicameral bone cysts are most common in the proximal humerus and femur. The lesions are most active during skeletal growth and usually heal spontaneously at maturity. Unicameral bone cysts often are asymptomatic, unless a pathological fracture has occurred. Plain radiographs reveal a centrally located, purely lytic lesion with a well-marginated outline.
Unicameral bone cysts are classified as active when they are within 1 cm of the physis and latent when they are closer to the diaphysis.

Reference: Page 40, Section: Unicameral Bone Cyst: True Cyst!

In these cases, the cartilage cap usually is more than 2 cm thick. (Best evaluated by MRI).

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about osteochondromatosis: (PGI Dec 01)

options.text: Usually affects long bones, but can also occur in skull and pelvis
Also known as multiple exostoses, diaphyseal aplasia
It doesn't interfere with general body stature

questions.answerText: Usually affects long bones, but can also occur in skull and pelvis; B. Usual site is metaphyseal region; C. Also known as multiple exostoses, diaphyseal aplasia; E. Autosomal dominant in inheritance
questions.explanation:
Osteochondromas are found on the metaphysics of a long bone near the physis they are seen most often on the distal femur, the proximal tibia, and the proximal humerus.
Multiple hereditary exostoses (diaphyseal aplasia) constitute an autosomal dominant (Chromosome 8, 11, 19 involved) condition with variable penetrance, disturbances in growth also occur.
Remember the fact that using the suffix 'tosis' means multiple lesions, e.g. osteochondromatosis means multiple osteochondromas. Osteochondromas can cause growth disturbances.

Reference: Page 42, Section: OSTEODNOROMA & Page 43, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

The typical patient with an osteoid osteoma has pain that is worse at night and is relieved by aspirin or other non- steroidal antiinflammatory medications.

Reference: Page 43, Section: OSTEODIOSTEOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Babu a 19-year-old male has a small circumscribed sclerotic swelling over diaphysis of femur; likely diagnosis is: (AIMS Nov 2001)
questions.explanation:
Well circumscribed sclerotic swelling over diaphysis of a long bone (femur) in a 19 years old suggests the diagnosis of osteoid osteoma.
Osteoid Osteoma-M.C.Femur Diaphysis.

Reference: Page 43, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 43, Section: OSTEODIOSTEOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: True about non-ossifying fibroma of bone: (PGI June 03); (PGI Dec 02)

options.text: Histologically giant cell with foam cell

questions.answerText: Eccentric; C. Sclerotic margin; D. Histologically giant cell with foam cell and E. Metaphyseal lesion.
questions.explanation:
FIBROUS CORTICAL DEFECT (NON-OSSIFYING FIBROMA): These are common developmental abnormalities and are believed to occur in 35% of children. Usually they are found incidentally. Generally, these lesions occur in the metaphyseal region of long bones in individuals 2-20 years old. Although any bone may be involved, femur is the commonest. On plain radiographs, a non- ossifying fibroma appears as a well- defined lobulated lesion located eccentrically in the metaphysis.

Reference: Page 43, Section: FIBROUS CORTICAL DEFECT (NON-OSSIFYING FIBROMA) & Page 44, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Mafucci Syndrome: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Maffucci syndrome is Enchondroma, subcutaneous hemangioma and phlebolith.

Reference: Page 44, Section: Enchondroma

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Most common tumor in bones of hand: (AllMS June 1997)
questions.explanation:
Enchondromas are most common type of hand bone tumor. - Phalanges of hand are involved most commonly and the proximal phalanx is the most common site.

Reference: Page 44, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy presented with painful swelling over the left shoulder. Radiograph of the shoulder showed an osteolytic area with stippled calcification over the proximal humeral epiphysis. Biopsy of the lesion revealed an immature fibrous matrix with scattered giant cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? (AllMS May 2013, Nov 2004)
questions.explanation:
Painful swelling over the left shoulder, osteolytic area and stippled calcification over proximal humeral epiphysis in a 15 years old suggest the diagnosis of chondroblastoma.

Reference: Page 44, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which one of the following bone tumors typically affects the epiphysis of a long bone? (AIIMS May 2005) (AIIMS May 2002)
questions.explanation:
Chondroblastoma occurs in the epiphysis of long bones before skeletal maturity.

Reference: Page 45, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Dense calcification is found in: (AIIMS May 2002)
questions.explanation:
You can simply solve this question by knowing very simple fact that punctate calcification is seen in cartilaginous tumors and amongst the given options. Only Chondroblastoma is cartilaginous.
In chondroblastomas Calcification is present and may surround individual cells, giving the classic "chicken wire" appearance.

Reference: Page 45, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 44, Section: CHONDROBLASTOMA/CODMAN'S TUMOR

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Soap bubble appearance on X-ray is seen in which bone tumor: (NEET Pattern 2013)
questions.explanation:
Soap bubble appearance*: Osteoclastoma (GCT), adamantinoma.
Soap bubble appearance at lower end of radius, the treatment of choice is: Excision and bone grafting.

Reference: Page 38, Section: Classical Radiological Features & Page 46, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following is epiphyseal tumor: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Epiphyseal: Osteoclastoma/Giant cell tumor (after physeal closure in adults).

Reference: Page 36, Section: MOST COMMON SITE OF PRIMARY BONE TUMORS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: GCT malignant component is: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Microscopically, giant cell tumors are composed of many multinucleated giant cells (typically 40-60 nuclei per cell) in a sea of mononuclear stromal cells (malignant cells).

Reference: Page 45, Section: GIANT CELL TUMOR (OSTEOCLASTOMA)

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following is a variant of giant cell tumor: (AIMS May 2011)
questions.explanation:
Eccentric lytic lesion with no calcification is the commonest differential. Ossifying fibroma, chondroblastoma and osteosarcoma will have calcification hence non-ossifying fibroma is a preferred answer here.
Note: Closest differential is ABC.

Reference: Page 46, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: The differential diagnosis of lesion, histologically resembling giant cell tumor in the small bones of the hands or feet, includes all of the following except: (AIMS May 06)
questions.explanation:
All mentioned tumor contain giant cells but osteosarcoma is extremely rare in short bones of hand and feet.
Giant cell variants (Tumor with giant cells): Brown tumor of hyper parathyroidism, Aneurysmal bone cyst (closest) and unicameral bone cyst, Non-ossifying fibroma (commonest) and Fibrous dysplasia, Osteoblastoma and Osteosarcoma, Metastatic carcinoma with giant cells, Chondromyxoid fibroma and Chondroblastoma, Pigmented villonodular synovitis (mostly occuring in knee), Benign fibrous histiocytoma, Malignant fibrous histiocytoma, Fibrosarcoma, Clear cell chondrosarcoma.

Reference: Page 46, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 45, Section: Giant cell variants

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Osteoclastoma is treated with: (PGI Dec 2K, PGI June 2001)
questions.answerText: Joint replacement; B. Excision; C. Curettage; D. Arthrodesis. Chemotherapy has no role in GCT.
questions.explanation:
Treatment of Osteoclastoma (GCT):
Extended Curettage by PMMA or phenol or liquid nitrogen and bone grafting - It is procedure of choice for most lesions.
Excision - Lower end of ulna, Upper end of fibula.
Excision and replacement by vascularized bone graft - Lower end of radius where upper end of fibula is grafted.
Excision and arthrodesis or prosthetic replacement or Turn-O-Plasty - Lower end femur and upper end tibia.
Treatment of recurrent lesions is the same as for primary lesions.
Amputation - Malignant recurrent GCT of extremity.
Radiotherapy - Spine (RT may cause malignant transformation of GCT).

Reference: Page 45, Section: Treatment of Osteoclastoma (GCT) & Page 46, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Soap bubble appearance at lower end of radius, the treatment of choice is: (AIMS June 1998)
questions.explanation:
Treatment of Osteoclastoma (GCT): 3. Excision and replacement by vascularized bone graft - Lower end of radius where upper end of fibula is grafted.
Soap bubble appearance*: Osteoclastoma (GCT).

Reference: Page 46, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 45, Section: Treatment of Osteoclastoma (GCT)

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Mandible most common tumor: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Please note that most common tumor of mandible is squamous cell carcinoma.

Reference: Page 46, Section: AMELOBLASTOMA & Page 47, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Characteristic radiological feature of fibrous dysplasia is: (AIMS May 2010)
questions.explanation:
Ground glass appearance: Fibrous Dysplasia.
In long bones, the fibrous dysplastic lesions have ground- glass appearance.

Reference: Page 38, Section: Classical Radiological Features & Page 47, Section: Radiographic Findings

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: True about Ameloblastoma: (PCI Dec 2006)
questions.explanation:
Most common site of ameloblastoma is mandible.
Most common site of ameloblastoma of long bones (i.e. adammatinooma) is Tibial diaphysis.
Adammatinooma is a slow growing benign locally aggressive tumor with late metastasis.
Well demarcated lytic (cystic) or mixed lytic/clerotic lesion involving the cortex.
It is a slow growing, locally invasive cystic benign tumor.

Reference: Page 47, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 46, Section: AMELOBLASTOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A33-year-old man presented with a slowly progressive swelling in the middle 1/3rd of his right tibia. X-rays examination revealed multiple sharply demarcated radiolucent lesions separated by areas of dense and sclerotic bone. Microscopic examination of a biopsy specimen revealed island of epithelial cells in a fibrous stroma. Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis? (AIMS May 2004)
questions.explanation:
ADAMANTINOMA-TIBIA: Adamantinoma is seen in second or third decade of life. It is almost exclusively found in tibial diaphysis.
The most common radiographic appearance is that of multiple, sharply demarcated radiolucent lesions in the tibial diaphysis. - Soap Bubble appearance.

Reference: Page 46, Section: ADAMANTINOMA-TIBIA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Most common site of admantinoma of the long bones is: (AIMS May 2002)
questions.explanation:
Ameloblastoma-Most common site mandible.
Ameloblastoma of long bones-Called adammatinooma and is most common in tibial diaphysis.

Reference: Page 47, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Most common site of origin of ameloblastoma is: (AIIMS Nov 2001)
questions.explanation:
Ameloblastoma is an epithelial tumor arising from ameloblast (enamel forming cell). The most common site is posterior mandible in the area of molar teeth.

Reference: Page 46, Section: AMELOBLASTOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Children with germline retinoblastoma are more likely to develop other primary malignancies in their later lifetime course. Which of the following can occur in such patients? (AIIMS Nov 2013)

options.text: Osteosarcoma of lower limbs and soft tissue sarcoma

questions.answerText: Osteosarcoma of lower limbs and soft tissue sarcoma
questions.explanation:
Osteosarcoma may be more common in patients with the hereditary form of retinoblastoma and Li-Fraumeni syndrome.

Reference: Page 47, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA & Page 49, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: X-ray appearance of osteosarcoma are all except: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Sun ray appearance*/ Codman's triangle: Osteosarcoma.
Soap bubble appearance*: Osteoclastoma (GCT), adamantinoma.

Reference: Page 38, Section: Classical Radiological Features

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Codman's is most commonly seen in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Codmans Triangle- Triangular bony growth seen at angle of lifting of periosteum it can be seen in any malignant lesion but usually osteosarcoma.

Reference: Page 15, Section: Types of Periosteal Reaction

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Codman's triangle and onion peel appearance are most commonly seen in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
In malignant lesions there is wide area of activity, e.g. Onion peel/codmans triangle and sunray appearance.
Onion peel or lamellated appearance- Seen in any malignant or chronic lesions (e.g. chronic osteomyelitis) but usually ewings sarcoma.
Codmans Triangle- Triangular bony growth seen at angle of lifting of periosteum it can be seen in any malignant lesion but usually osteosarcoma.

Reference: Page 15, Section: Types of Periosteal Reaction

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Matrix forming tumor is: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Osteosarcoma is a tumor characterized by the production of osteoid matrix by malignant cells.

Reference: Page 47, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Osteosarcoma most commonly affects: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Most primary osteosarcomas occur at the sites of the most rapid bone growth, including the distal femur, the proximal tibia, and the proximal humerus.
Most common site of Osteogenic sarcoma is: Femur lower end.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA & Page 37, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Radiation induced tumor: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Although osteosarcoma is the most common radiation-induced sarcoma, fibrosarcoma and malignant fibrous histiocytoma also are relatively common in this setting.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following malignant tumors is radioresistant? (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
It is highly radio resistant and ideally treated by chemotherapy followed by limb salvage surgery/amputation followed by chemotherapy.
Most primary bone malignancies are relatively radio resistant. Exceptions are the marrow cell tumors, including multiple myeloma, lymphoma, and Ewing sarcoma, which are each exquisitely sensitive.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA & Page 39, Section: Radiation Therapy

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following is a pulsatile tumor: (AIIMS May 2010)
questions.explanation:
Pulsatile bone tumors in following order answer must be preferred. Osteosarcoma > ABC > Angioendothelioma of bone > G.C.T. Amongst metastasis renal and thyroid have pulsatile metastasis.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: True about osteosarcoma: (PGI Nov 2009)

options.text: Most commonly involve knee and distal femur
Spread to lung through hematogenous route
Exclusively found in adolescent and early adult life

questions.answerText: Most commonly involve knee and distal femur; C. Spread to lung through hematogenous route; E. X-ray: sunray appearance.
questions.explanation:
Most primary osteosarcomas occur at the sites of the most rapid bone growth, including the distal femur, the proximal tibia, and the proximal humerus.
The lungs are the most common sites of metastases.
X-ray has sunray appearance.
Osteosarcoma: Onset can occur at any age; however, primary high-grade osteosarcoma occurs most commonly in the second decade of life.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA & Page 49, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 8-year-male progressive swelling upper end tibia - irregular, local temperature raised, variable consistency and ill defined margins: (DPG 2009)
questions.explanation:
The clinical presentation in question can occur both in Ewing's sarcoma and osteosarcoma. History of trivial trauma, Progressive swelling, Raised local temperature, Variable consistency, ill defined margins. However, swelling is around the knee joint at upper end of tibia, which favours the diagnosis of osteosarcoma (metaphyseal lesion). Ewing's sarcoma usually occurs in the diaphysis of the bone (middle of the shaft).

Reference: Page 49, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: 'T'-10 Protocol' for treatment of osteosarcoma includes all of the following, except: (AI 2009)
questions.explanation:
Note: Etoposide is not included in the T-10 protocol for osteosarcoma.
Rosens T-10 Protocol for osteosarcoma: Patients were treated with high-dose methotrexate (HDMTX) and citrovorum factor rescue (CFR), Adriamycin, and the combination of bleomycin, cyclophosphamide and dactinomycin (BCD) given for 4-6 weeks prior to definitive surgery.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA & Page 49, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: All of the following investigations are needed for the diagnosis of osteosarcoma, except: (All India 2007)
questions.explanation:
A biopsy of the lesion (not bone marrow biopsy) should always be carried out before commencing treatment.
MRI is the best test to measure the extent of the tumor within the bone and in the soft tissue and to determine the relationship of the tumor to nearby anatomical structures.
A bone scan should be obtained to look for skeletal metastases, and radiographs and CT scans of the chest should be done to search for pulmonary metastases.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA & Page 49, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Management plan for osteogenic sarcoma of the lower end of femur must include: (AI 2004)
questions.explanation:
It is highly radio resistant and ideally treated by chemotherapy followed by limb salvage surgery/amputation followed by chemotherapy.

Reference: Page 48, Section: OSTEOSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following bone tumor present secondaries in lung with pneumothorax: (AIIMS Sept 1996, AIIMS Dec 1995)
questions.explanation:
Both osteogenic sarcoma and Ewing's sarcoma may have metastasis to lung.
However it is much more common in osteogenic sarcoma and about 10% of patients have pulmonary metastasis by the time they are first seen. Incidence of pneumothorax is higher in osteosarcoma metastasis.

Reference: Page 49, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy presents with swelling and pain over tibia. On X-ray there is peristoreal reaction in diaphysis. Probable diagnosis is: (A/IMS May 2014)
questions.explanation:
Diaphysis + Periosteal reaction = Ewing's sarcoma.
Classically, Ewing sarcoma appears radiographically as a destructive lesion in the diaphysis of a long bone with an "onion skin" periosteal reaction.

Reference: Page 50, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Most common site of Ewing's sarcoma:(NEET Pattern 2013)
questions.explanation:
Ewing's sarcoma: Femur (Most common site).
Most common site of Ewing's sarcoma: Shaft of femur.

Reference: Page 36, Section: Most common sites & Page 50, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Maximum Incidence of Ewing's occurs in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Ewing sarcoma is the fourth most common primary malignancy of bone, but it is the second most common (after osteosarcoma) in patients younger than 30 years of age and the most common in patients younger than 10 years of age. Its maximum incidence is seen in 2nd decade of life.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Small round cell tumor among the following: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Diaphyseal: 1. Round cell lesions—Ewing's sarcoma.

Reference: Page 36, Section: MOST COMMON SITE OF PRIMARY BONE TUMORS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Glycogen Positive cells are seen in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
In addition, Ewing sarcomas usually are periodic acid- Schiff positive (owing to intracellular glycogen) and reticulin negative.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Mass in anterior aspect of thigh fixed to bone the procedure to be carried out: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Biopsy: It is the gold standard for any tumor.

Reference: Page 38, Section: Important Notes

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Ewing's most common age group: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Its maximum incidence is seen in 2nd decade of life.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: 1st decade most common bone tumor: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
1st decade usually ewing's sarcoma.
Ewing sarcoma is the most common in patients younger than 10 years of age.

Reference: Page 37, Section: AGE PREDILECTION & Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: PAS positive cells are seen in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
In addition, Ewing sarcomas usually are periodic acid- Schiff positive (owing to intracellular glycogen) and reticulin negative.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Mic 2 positive cells are seen in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
MIC2(CD99) is a specific marker for Ewing's sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumors and is expressed on short- arm of chromosome x and y.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: CD 99 is marker of: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
MIC2(CD99) is a specific marker for Ewing's sarcoma and peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumors.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Ewing's Sarcoma is associated with which genetic defect: (Al2012)
questions.explanation:
The t(11; 22) (q24; q12) is the most common translocation diagnostic of Ewing sarcoma and is present in greater than 90% of cases. Other diagnostic translocations, including t(21; 22) (q22; q12), t(7; 22) (p22; q12), trisomy 8 and trisomy 12.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Poor prognostic sign for ewing's sarcoma is: (AIIMS Non 2010)
questions.explanation:
The worst prognostic factor is the presence of distant metastases.
Fever, anemia, and elevation of laboratory values (white blood cell count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, lactate dehydrogenase) have been reported to indicate more extensive disease and a worse prognosis.
Older age at presentation (with a cutoff around 12-15 years old) and male gender also have been reported to be associated with a worse prognosis.
Histological grade is of no prognostic significance because all Ewing sarcomas are considered high grade.

Reference: Page 50, Section: EWING SARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy with h/o trauma 2 months back now presents with fever and acute pain over thigh. On X-ray femoral shaft shows lesions with multiple laminated periosteal reaction next line of management: (AIIMS Nov 09)
questions.explanation:
Information in this question are: 1st Decade, diaphyseal lesion with onion peel reaction goes towards Ewing's sarcoma. Next best investigation is MRI for soft tissue involvement, marrow involvement and micrometastasis. Overall the best investigation is Biopsy to confirm the diagnosis but MRI is done before the biopsy, to localize the best site for biopsy.

Reference: Page 51, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy is injured while playing cricket. X-rays of the leg rule out a possible fracture. The radiologist reports the boy has an evidence of aggressive bone tumor with both bone destruction and soft tissue mass. The bone biopsy reveals a bone cancer with neural differentiation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? (AIIMS May 2006)
questions.explanation:
Ewing's sarcoma is part of a family of peripheral neuroectodermal tumors (PNET) that share a common cytogenetic translocation of chromosomes 11 and 22, t(11:22.), differing only in their degree of neural differentiation, Ewing's sarcoma is poorly differentiated where as PNET exhibits definite neural differentiation.

Reference: Page 51, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Chordoma commonly involves: (PCI June 02)
questions.explanation:
Chordoma: Sacrum (most common) > sphenooccipital region (clivus) > anterior vertebral body, i.e. involves only axial skeleton.
Greater than 50% of chordomas arise in the sacrococcygeal area, and more than 30% arise at the base of the skull.

Reference: Page 36, Section: Most common sites & Page 51, Section: CHORDOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following is not a benign bone tumor: (Al1996)
questions.explanation:
Chordoma is a malignant tumor arising from notochordal remnants.

Reference: Page 51, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 51, Section: CHORDOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Tumor with calcification is seen in: (Neet Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
Malignant are preferred over Benign lesions.
The pattern of calcification has been described as "punctate", "popcorn", or "comma-shaped".

Reference: Page 52, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS & Page 51, Section: CHONDROSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following tumor is associated with hyperglycemia? (Al 2010)
questions.explanation:
Chondrosarcoma can produce hyperglycemia in 85% cases.

Reference: Page 51, Section: CHONDROSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 45 years male presented with an expansile lesion in the centre of femoral metaphysis. The lesion shows endosteal scalloping and punctuate calcifications. Most likely diagnosis is: (Al 2002)
questions.explanation:
The radiographic appearance of chondrosarcoma frequently is similar to enchondroma, it is a lesion arising in the medullary cavity with irregular matrix calcification. The pattern of calcification has been described as "punctate", "popcorn", or "comma-shaped". Compared with enchondroma, however, chondrosarcoma has a more aggressive appearance with bone destruction, cortical erosions, periosteal reaction, and rarely a soft- tissue mass. A CT scan can be helpful to show endosteal erosions or other evidence of a destructive lesion and to differentiate benign from malignant cartilage lesions.

Reference: Page 51, Section: CHONDROSARCOMA

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Striated Vertebra are seen in: (NEET Pattern 2012)
questions.explanation:
The radiographic appearance in the spine usually is characteristic, with thickened, vertically oriented trabeculae giving the classic "jailhouse" (Corduroy) appearance.
Striated Vertebra are seen in Hemangioma.

Reference: Page 52, Section: HAEMANGIOMA OF BONE & Page 52, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding hemangioma of the bone: (PCI Dec 01)

options.text: Requires observation as it is premalignant
Local gigantism occurs when it occurs in an extremity

questions.answerText: Occurs commonly in skull bones; C. Hamartomatous in origin; E. Local gigantism occurs when it occurs in an extremity.
questions.explanation:
Hemangioma is a common benign bone lesion. It is estimated that 10% of the population has asymptomatic hemangioma of the vertebral bodies. Hemangiomas also are common in the skull. They usually are discovered as incidental findings.
Treatment usually is not necessary.

Reference: Page 52, Section: HAEMANGIOMA OF BONE & Page 52, Section: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

questions.src: Orthopedics Quick Review, 3/e · Chapter 4: Orthopedics Oncology
questions.stem: A 70-year-old male complaints of multiple bone pains, on evaluation he has high ESR, high Calcium values, lytic lesion in multiple bones >20% plasma cells in peripheral smear. Most likely diagnosis is? (AIIMS May 2013)

Grade I: Clean wound of <1 cm length
Grade II: Wound >1 cm in length without extensive soft tissue damage, skin flap or avulsion
Grade III: Wound associated with extensive soft tissue damage, comminution, contamination or segmental fractures
Grade IIIA: Adequate periosteal coverage is there
Grade IIIB: Significant periosteal stripping and it requires secondary bone coverage procedure like skin grafting or flap
Grade IIIC: Open fracture with Vascular injury that requires vascular repair

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the crush syndrome: (AIIMS May 02)
questions.explanation:
Pathophysiology: Due to ischemia, tissues die and accumulate toxic metabolites. When limb is freed, reperfusion injury occurs due to reactive oxygen metabolites. The ion pumps in the capillary and muscle cells fail, leading to fluid shifts which cause swelling leading to compartment syndrome and further ischemia. Toxic metabolites (myohaemoglobin) are released into circulation resulting: 1. Rhabdomyolysis, 2. Hypocalcemia, 3. Hyperuricemia, 4. Hyperphosphatemia, 5. Hyperkalemia <- Cardiac arrest, 6. Cardiomyopathy, 7. Myoglobinemia and myoglobinuria, 8. Metabolic acidosis, 9. Acute tubular necrosis and ARF, 10. DIC.

Reference: Page 49, Section: CRUSH SYNDROME

Forced mannitol alkaline diuresis is maintained until myoglobin is no longer detected in urine. If oliguria persists, renal dialysis will be needed.
